description: Hottel-Whillier-Bliss with U_L(T) thermal loss curve. F1b extends F1a (constant U_L) with a weak temperature-dependent U_L(DeltaT) for vacuum insulation. Also adds incidence angle modifier (IAM) for off-normal performance.

unit.name: Generic 30-tube Evacuated Tube Collector (Apricus AP-30 style)
unit.source: Duffie & Beckman (2013), 'Solar Engineering of Thermal Processes', 4th ed., Ch.6; SRCC OG-100 ETC ratings; ISO 9806:2017 second-order efficiency equation

eta_0.note: Zero-loss optical efficiency (= F_R * tau * alpha at normal incidence)

a1.note: First-order heat loss coefficient F_R*U_L at zero DeltaT

a2.note: Second-order heat loss coefficient for vacuum insulation. VERY small: ETC vacuum limits conduction/convection so a2 << flat plate (~0.06). Weak T dependence from end-cap conduction and residual gas.

b0.note: IAM incidence angle modifier coefficient (Duffie & Beckman Eq. 6.17.6)

unit.note_a2: RATIONALE: For evacuated tube collectors, the second-order loss coefficient a2 is much smaller than for flat-plate collectors (~0.06 W/m2K2) because vacuum insulation eliminates most convective loss. The residual a2=0.012 accounts for end-cap conduction and residual gas conduction at temperatures above ~100C. Certified values from SRCC for high-performance ETCs are in range 0.008-0.020 W/m2K2.

T_inlet.note: ETCs operate at higher T than flat plate
